maria_h: Heads-up: following RFC merge — need a quick sync on Dedicated GPU pool scaling contracts and operator guardrails. TL;DR: operator should enforce SLO budget, but app teams get explicit soft/hard reservations. Proposed flow below.

sanjay_k: 👍 what's the expected API shape? Admission only, or do we expose a subresource for leases?

maria_h: idea: two APIs: (1) Reservation contract (long-lived) -> tenant declares min-qps/min-throughput and max-cost-band; (2) Lease API (short-lived) -> operator grants ephemeral leases for burst lanes. Reservations influence headroom.

liam_r: sounds good. Questions: eviction semantics during node drain? Should reservations be sacrosanct? If infra needs to reclaim for infra-critical jobs, can we preempt?

tasha: propose preemption tiers: reserved_hard (no preempt unless emergency), reserved_soft (preempt with 5m warning), best-effort (no guarantees). Operator respects tiers and emits events.

andre_w: @maria_h +1 on tiers. Also we need a cost-accounting ledger per lease to debit tenant credits. Otherwise tenants will hog burst for free.

maria_h: yep. ledger + token-bucket style quota suggested. Also require tenant-supplied backoff hooks so we can signal clients to degrade quality gracefully.

ops-bot: deploy noticed: autoscaler v2 alpha rolled to canary on staging cluster. Logs: `scale_loop.go: warn: headroom mismatch for pool=a2.small`

liam_r: how aggressive should autoscaler be w.r.t. ramp rate? We saw oscillation at 20s scale windows before.

sanjay_k: propose two knobs: rate_limit (nodes/min) and hysteresis window (seconds). default rate_limit=1 node/2m and hysteresis=120s.

tasha: plus cooldown after eviction events (double the hyst window) to avoid thrashing.

andre_w: on operator boundary: who owns decision to drain? operator signals intent, but runtime should own graceful session migration. Keep operator minimal: mark node unschedulable and emit `drain-intent` event.

maria_h: agree. Runtime subscribes to event and initiates KV cache checkpointing + model shard migration. Document handshake: `intent -> prepare -> ready -> evict` 4-state transition.

liam_r: small nit: we need a fallback when `prepare` stalls (e.g., tenant runtime crashes). operator should have TTL -> force-evict after X.

maria_h: TTL default 7m, adjustable per-reservation class. Also add `reason` codes for evictions for observability.

sanjay_k: can we simulate cost impact in staging? I'd like to run a chaos job that marks 30% nodes unsched and measure 99p latency.

maria_h: yes, i'll spin up a canary test plan and add to eng-runtime CI.

andre_w: final ask: document migration APIs and add an audit trail for billing. I'll draft an RFC appendix.

maria_h: thanks all, creating follow-up issue: infra#4537 with action items: API shape, operator event schema, ledger design, canary plan.

infra-bot: created issue infra#4537 by maria_h

tasha: awesome, ping me when issue is live — will add SLO matrices.

sanjay_k: will add autoscaler sim metrics.

maria_h: closing thread for now, we'll iterate in the issue. :shipit:
